newsitem.title: BOSNIA: ICRC reports little progress in search for missing.
newsitem.headline: ICRC reports little progress in search for missing.

text.p: Bosnian authorities are dragging their feet over requests to track down thousands of people who went missing during the country's 1992-95 war, international aid officials reported on Tuesday.

The International Committee of the Red Cross has received 18,500 queries from families searching for missing relatives but Bosnian Serb and Moslem-Croat authorities have only responded in some 1,000 cases.
"We are not advancing enough on this question", Nina Winquist-Galbe, a spokesperson for the ICRC, told a news conference.
Governments in Bosnia's Serb entity and Moslem-Croat federation bear the primary responsibility for providing information on missing persons to the ICRC.
But rival authorities have linked queries for missing persons to other issues or provided lists of dead which fail to correspond to requests relayed by the ICRC.
The ICRC launched a television and radio campaign this month to draw attention to the plight of families who lack information about the whereabouts of their relatives, Winquist-Galbe said.

Bosnian families deserved an answer to their queries after enduring "unbearable uncertainty" about the fate of their loved ones, said Marguerite Contat Hickel, an ICRC official who heads up efforts to trace those missing.
"I have to stress that since the peace agreement very few answers were given to the ICRC by the relevant authorities," Hickel said in a statement.
"The ICRC feels the time has come to gear up the process by launching this media campaign and to remind the families that the ICRC continues to work on their behalf."
